title: The court's role in appointing an arbitrator when parties disagree
p1: What happens when two parties agree to settle disputes through arbitration but cannot agree on the person who will decide the case? Many assume the entire process comes to a standstill. But the law has a solution.
p2: A common misconception is that courts take over arbitration when parties disagree. The reality is different. The court’s role is usually limited to helping appoint an arbitrator when the agreed process fails. It does not decide the dispute itself.
p3: This means arbitration can continue even when cooperation breaks down. The court acts as a facilitator, ensuring that one party cannot delay the process simply by refusing to agree on an arbitrator. The bigger lesson: dispute resolution agreements work best when there is a clear path for handling disagreements.
conclusion: Did you know that a court can step in to appoint an arbitrator without taking control of the arbitration itself? Do you think this balance between party choice and court intervention works well?
